titleEn: It's Okay to Cry—Wipe with Your Scarf!

pages.text: "I'll play with you all day!" Yuki hugged a straw doll and hopped across the yard. Overnight rain had made its edge muddy. Brown dog Momo followed closely.
A hop, then a slip—Yuki fell into the mud. The dropped doll sank deep. Yuki's chin trembled.
Tears were coming, but Yuki bit their lip. "I won't cry. It doesn't hurt." Yuki turned away. Holding back made their throat ache and nose sting.
Grandma came down from the porch in her gray layered clothes and knelt before Yuki. "Your knee hurts, and your doll is wet." "...Yes." Yuki's shoulders shook.
Grandma lifted the scarf's end and wiped Yuki's eyes. "Cry if you want. You have something to wipe with right here." Tears dropped one by one.
"Waaah!" Yuki wrapped both arms around Grandma's waist and buried their face in her clothes. She patted the shaking back. "It's Okay to Cry—Wipe with Your Scarf!"
Yuki held the scarf's end and rubbed their cheeks. Wet cheeks dried, and raised shoulders settled down. "Oh? It doesn't hurt anymore."
Momo brought the muddy doll in their mouth and dropped it at Yuki's feet. Yuki hugged it and rubbed cheeks against it. "You were startled, too, weren't you?" Yuki wiped its face with the scarf.
A few days later, the doll's arm came off. Before the porch, Yuki spread both arms. "One, hold my scarf's end! Two, let tears out if they come! Three, open my arms!" "Grandma, I'm sad!"
Grandma wrapped Yuki in both arms and rested her chin on their head. After crying, the aching throat relaxed. "It's Okay to Cry—Wipe with Your Scarf!" The scarf's end poked out between them.
